blocks.text: Quantifiers are used in predicate logic to describe how many objects satisfy a condition. They help us make general statements or statements about specific objects. Quantifiers make predicate logic more powerful than propositional logic. Using quantifiers, we can write statements like “All students are hardworking” or “Some books are interesting.” Quantifiers help represent knowledge clearly and precisely.

blocks.title: Tidbit
blocks.text: Quantifiers like “for all” or “there exists” help us express general rules or possibilities clearly.
